newsitem.title: USA: U.S. seeks experts to assess Elk Hills field value.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seeks experts to assess Elk Hills field value.

text.p: U.S. Energy Department issued a notice Wednesday seeking five experts to assess the value of its Elk Hills oil field, which it must sell by February 1998.

Under a 1996 law calling for the sale of the government's 78 percent stake in the oil and gas field, expected to be one of the largest federal privatization's ever, the department must use five independent assessments to set the threshold for minimum acceptable bids.
The field is among the 10 largest in the lower 48 states.

To qualify for consideration, a company must operate in the United States and must have participated since Jan 1, 1993, in at least one U.S. or international oil or gas field evaluation worth at least $100 million, an Energy Department official said.
The company must also have background in estimating environmental clean-up and restoration costs.
Teams may qualify if at least one member meets the qualifications.
Experts "will be precluded from advising bidders in the actual sale of the field," the official said.
Companies selected are expected to complete the assessment by September 1997.
Energy Department plans to announce within the next two weeks its preliminary sales strategy for the field, which is co-owned by Chevron Corp.
